correctness.rationale: For each pair of integers d>=2 and 1<=s<=d, the signed-sparse-Dirichlet face law yields Gram diag(1,2/[d(s+1)] repeated d times). The reproducing kernel is 1+[d(s+1)/2]x dot y, and exact integration of the Beta(1,s-1) excess tail gives the claimed norm. The K(v,.) and K(w,.) sign disagreement on positive-measure face neighborhoods near -v proves strict vertex-only norming and the sign-kernel input extremizers. The strict inequality log(1-u)>-u/(1-u) gives positive derivative of the continuous rank interpolation and strict rank monotonicity. The independent radial Beta decomposition of solid volume yields its covariance, exact kernel norm, vertex classification and strict volume-versus-boundary comparison; the latter uses Jensen and E[R]>E[R^2]. A bounded quadratic binomial remainder yields the stated uniform O(1/d) and half-step bound and limiting difference 1/2. Actual standalone checker, using exact rational beta-density expansion, passed 594 dimension/rank integrals, but universal proof is analytic.

originality.rationale: Comparison of complete mathematical claims gives no domination by the accessible source results. Exact simplex solid-volume norms do not imply cross-polytope face-skeleton norms. The existing general cone-boundary versus volume strict inequality for centrally symmetric bodies yields only the last order relation and not the new all-skeleton constants, exact extremizers, uniform half-step law or sharp cross-polytope gap. Full texts of Oswald (2006) and Hangelbroek et al. (2010) were inspected at their precise result sections; both concern other projection spaces and settings. Ranked face-skeleton exact constants were not found in multiple targeted mathematical literature and indexed-record searches. Residual possibility of an unindexed equivalent treatment remains.
residual_risks: An equivalent exact calculation may exist in unindexed approximation or optimal-design literature. The indexed simplex-affine full text was inaccessible, although its abstract theorem addresses another polytope and measure.
This is a same-model comparison, not a formally independent priority audit.

value.rationale: All equal-rank face skeleta of a regular cross-polytope are canonical sampling supports for multivariate affine least squares, linking finite vertex observations, lower-dimensional strata, boundary sampling and solid sampling. The complete sharp norm ladder and strict classification of all extremal evaluation locations quantify a systematic and initially counterintuitive increase in worst-case amplification as observations move to larger-dimensional faces. Every rank contributes an asymptotically uniform half-unit increase, and the remaining volume step has a nonvanishing exact 1/2 limit. These are natural all-rank invariant values and stability information not supplied by the old general cone-versus-volume comparison; no arbitrary parameter slice or tiny numerical improvement is used.
